description: Hygiene ratchet tests reject valid strict improvements (shrinking overridden modules and removing inline # noqa suppressions) while holon-config/hygiene/module_budgets.json is frozen.
goal: Update tests/test_module_budgets.py and tests/test_complexity_baseline.py so shrinking an overridden module under frozen holon-config/hygiene/module_budgets.json or removing inline # noqa suppressions passes CI cleanly while budget or complexity regressions still fail. Specifically: (1) update test_live_repository_passes_module_budgets in tests/test_module_budgets.py to assert main(...) == 0 and captured.err == "" without failing on informational 'Ratchet notice:' stdout lines, while preserving failure checks when a module exceeds its budget or main returns non-zero; (2) update test_complexity_baseline_ratchet_ceiling in tests/test_complexity_baseline.py to enforce total_count <= BASELINE_CEILING without failing when inline # noqa suppressions strictly decrease below BASELINE_CEILING; (3) add unit tests in both test files proving shrinking an overridden module passes while emitting a ratchet notice and reducing # noqa count below ceiling passes while exceeding ceiling fails. Use zero docstrings and zero comments in all modified files and NEVER modify holon-config/hygiene/module_budgets.json. Code is self-explaining: no docstrings and no comments except '# why:' comments that record a reason the code cannot show.
rationale: Allowing monotonic improvements in module sizes and inline # noqa counts unblocks refactor flows without weakening upper-bound budget or complexity enforcement.
acceptance_criteria: tests/test_module_budgets.py::test_live_repository_passes_module_budgets asserts main(...) == 0 and captured.err == "" without failing on informational Ratchet notice: stdout lines, while still failing if any module exceeds its budget or main(...) returns non-zero.

tests/test_complexity_baseline.py::test_complexity_baseline_ratchet_ceiling enforces total_count <= BASELINE_CEILING without failing when inline # noqa suppressions strictly decrease below BASELINE_CEILING.

Unit tests prove both behaviors (shrinking an overridden module passes while emitting a ratchet notice; reducing # noqa count below ceiling passes while exceeding ceiling fails), uv run pytest and uv run task lint pass with zero docstrings/comments, and holon-config/hygiene/module_budgets.json is untouched.
